subject.title: Feature Request: Configurable Session Lane Concurrency + Auto-Yield

question: Should OpenClaw add public session-lane concurrency and auto-yield config, or should same-session responsiveness be solved through a scheduler/fairness model without widening concurrent session writers?
rationale: The requested behavior changes session ordering, transcript/write-lock safety, active-run ownership, cancellation, and public config surface, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Design Scheduler Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, land or replace the diagnostics-threshold slice separately, and design foreground/background priority, interrupt, and yield semantics before implementation.

options.title: Accept Direct Config Knobs
options.body: Add session concurrency and auto-yield settings only after maintainers define compatibility defaults, upgrade behavior, tests, docs, and safety limits for same-session parallelism.

options.title: Decline Concurrency Config
options.body: Leave sessions serialized by design and improve responsiveness through existing queue modes, steering, interrupt, and explicit sessions_yield guidance instead.

recommendation.title: Design Scheduler Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, land or replace the diagnostics-threshold slice separately, and design foreground/background priority, interrupt, and yield semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current and historical connection to the command queue, gateway lane application, and scheduler docs that this decision would change.
